newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms to pump Papua New Guinea oil from 1998.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms to pump Papua New Guinea oil from 1998.

text.p: Oil firms Japan Energy Corp and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd said on Friday in separate statements they would start producing oil in Papua New Guinea from 1998, as members of a $300 million project.
The Gobe project, led by U.S. Chevron Corp, will develop the South-East Gobe field and the Gobe Main field.
Potential reserves are estimated at a combined 93 million barrels, and peak production is planned at 50,000 barrels-per-day (bpd), Mitsubishi Oil said.
Production is due to start in the first quarter of 1998, using existing facilities from the nearby Kutubu oil field, Mitsubishi Oil said.
A Japanese conglomerate, of which a Japan Energy subsidiary is a member, has development rights to the South East Gobe field and will receive about 4,400 barrels-per-day of crude.
About 2,000 bpd will be earmarked for Mitsubishi Oil, which has rights to the South-East Gobe and the Gobe Main oil field.

The two fields are to be jointly developed because the South-East Gobe field straddles the boundary between prospecting licences PPL-161, where the Gobe Main field is located, and PPL-56, the statements said.
Other participants to the Gobe project include the Papua New Guinea government, Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd, Ampolex Ltd and Oil Search Ltd, the statements said.
